chunk_findings.detail:
The guard that is meant to prevent a summary-borne lesson from being dropped against an in-import record that itself will not be imported only inspects records *already processed* (`dropped` is filled while iterating `mine` in `plan.found` order). When the in-import target is later in the list than the summary, `id(tgt) in dropped` is still False, so the summary is dropped against a record that is subsequently dropped too, and the note claims it duplicates something "in this import" that never gets imported. This makes the outcome order-dependent, and the note can reference a non-imported record.

Concrete input: `plan.found` contains, in this order, a summary–tagged lesson `S`, a non-summary lesson `A`, and the queue already holds lesson `Q`; `A` scores 0.80 against `Q`, `S` scores 0.80 against `A`, and `S` scores 0.60 against `Q` (below `ask_threshold`). Processing `S` first: `A` is in `in_plan` and `is_summary(A)` is False, so the guard passes, `S` is dropped with `where="import"` and `of=A`; then `A` is dropped against `Q`. Both are removed, and the operator's note says `S` duplicates `A`, which is not being imported. Now put `A` before `S` in the file: `A` is dropped against `Q` first; then for `S`, the candidate `A` hits `id(tgt) in dropped` and is skipped, `Q` scores 0.60 < `ask_threshold`, so `S` is imported. The same file content therefore imports different records depending only on the order the records appear, and in one ordering the reported "in this import" duplicate target is a record that was itself removed.

chunk_findings.detail: The two adjacent assertions in `test_a_summary_bullet_that_repeats_a_lesson_is_reported_not_imported` disagree on case. Line 71 checks the rebase slug case-insensitively (`"rebase" in i.lower()`), but line 72 checks the cache slug case-sensitively (`"cache" in i`). The summary bullet that should be imported is `**Cache keys.** …`; if the importer derives the generated id from the bullet title (which the same assertion presupposes, since it looks for a title word inside an `LS-…` id), the id will be e.g. `LS-Cache-keys`, and `"cache" in "LS-Cache-keys"` is `False`. The assertion then fails with `the new bullet imports` even though the cache bullet *was* imported, i.e. the test reports a false failure for a correct implementation. Line 72 needs the same `i.lower()` treatment as line 71 (or the id generator must be proven to lower-case slugs, which line 71's defensive `.lower()` suggests it is not).

chunk_findings.detail: `_resolve_chains` rewrites `d.of`/`d.where` to the finally-held record, but it leaves `d.identical` (and `d.score`) at the value computed against the *intermediate* import record. A chain hop through a near-duplicate is therefore reported as a word-for-word repeat. Concrete case: the import has a summary bullet `S` whose text is byte-identical to an imported lesson `B`, and `B` is only a near-duplicate (score ≥ `ask_threshold`, `"identical"` not set) of an already-held lesson `C`. `S` matches `B` first (score 1.0, `identical=True`), so `dropped[id(S)] = Duplicate(S, "B", 1.0, True, "import")`; `_resolve_chains` then sets `S.of = "C"`, `S.where = "queue"` but leaves `S.identical = True`. `S` is not identical to `C` (the `B`→`C` hop was a near match only), yet `same = [d for d in plan.duplicates if d.identical]` picks it up and the note asserts `S = C` as a word-for-word repeat, while `S` is silently dropped and never appears in the near-duplicate list the operator is supposed to adjudicate (`near = [... if not d.identical]`). This bypasses the design rule that near-duplicates must be listed for a decision, and prints a false claim ("repeat existing ones word for word") about a pair that only scores, say, 0.85. The same staleness makes the shown score for resolved entries belong to the wrong comparison.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer.py `_resolve_chains` / `_dedupe_found`

chunk_findings.detail:
`_resolve_chains` rewrites `Duplicate.of` / `Duplicate.where` to point at the record that is
actually held, but it leaves the match classification (`d.identical`) and `d.score` computed
against the *immediate* candidate. The result is a user-facing note that can claim an exact,
word-for-word repeat against a record the record only near-matches.

Concrete input: a plan whose summary bullet `A` has text identical to another record of the
same import, lesson `B`, where `B` itself only near-matches an already-held record `C`
(score 0.85 ≥ `ask_threshold`, so `B` is dropped). When `A` is assessed, `similar.assess`
returns candidates ordered by descending score, so `B` (score 1.0, `identical` flag) comes
before `C` (0.85). `B` is an import target and `A` is a summary while `B` is not, so
`dropped[id(A)] = Duplicate(A, B.ident, 1.0, identical=True, "import")`. `B` is separately
dropped against `C` (`identical=False`). `_resolve_chains` then sets `A.of = C` and
`A.where = "queue"` while `A.identical` stays `True` and `A.score` stays `1.0`. The `same`
note therefore prints:

    1 record(s) repeat existing ones word for word and were not imported: A = C

which is false: `A` is not word-for-word equal to `C` (only `B` ~ `C`), so the operator is
told `A` is an exact duplicate of `C` and does not review `A`'s content. The same staleness
applies to the near-duplicate list, where `d.score` is the score against the pre-resolution
target (e.g. it reports `A ~ C (0.90` using `A`~`B`'s score, not `A`~`C`'s 0.85).

Relatedly, the identical note's wording is unconditionally "repeat existing ones" even when
`_resolve_chains` leaves `d.where == "import"` (the target is a record of this very import,
not an existing one), so the printed claim is wrong there too.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/importer.py:_resolve_chains` / `_dedupe_found`

chunk_findings.detail: The identical-duplicate report does not distinguish a target that is held in the queue from a target that is merely another record of the same import. A summary-born lesson `S` whose text is identical to a non-summary lesson `L` in the same file (with `L` itself new and therefore kept) is dropped with `where == "import"`; `_resolve_chains` cannot advance it because `id(in_plan[L])` is not in `dropped`, so `where` stays `"import"`. It therefore lands in `same = [d for d in plan.duplicates if d.identical]` and is rendered by the `same` note as `f"{d.found.ident} = {d.of}"` under the header "repeat ones already held word for word". In this input `L` is not held at all — it is being imported by this very run — so the note tells the operator a sibling record was "already held" and hides that the duplicate is inside the import. The near-duplicate branch handles exactly this situation by consulting `d.where` and appending `", in this import"`, but the identical branch never looks at `d.where`, so the two halves of the report disagree about what "already held" means. Concretely: a file containing a new full lesson `L30` plus a summary bullet whose text is copied verbatim from `L30` produces the note `"1 record(s) repeat ones already held word for word and were not imported: S = L30"`, which is false about `L30`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer.py:_dedupe_found (identical-note block)

chunk_findings.detail:
Input: an import file whose log is empty (the first import of a file) containing a lesson `L` and a generated summary bullet `S` whose title/body is verbatim `L`. The matcher reports `S` as `identical` to the in-import record `L`, so `dropped[id(S)] = Duplicate(S, "L", ..., identical=True, where="import")`. `L` itself is not dropped (nothing is held yet), so it stays in `plan.found` and is imported by this same run; the chain resolver does not rewrite `S.of`/`S.where` because `id(in_plan["L"])` is not in `dropped`. The note then renders:

    "1 record(s) repeat ones already held word for word and were not imported: S = L"

`L` is not "already held" at review time — it is one of the records this very import is about to create. The sibling near-duplicate branch explicitly distinguishes this case (`', in this import' if d.where == 'import'`), but the identical branch does not, so the onboarding conversation misreports the provenance of the named target for exactly the scenario this change targets (a summary bullet repeating a lesson). The consequence is that an operator reviewing the proposal is told the target already exists in the log when the log is empty and the target is part of the pending proposal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer.py:_dedupe_found (identical-duplicates note)

chunk_findings.detail: `in_plan` is keyed by `f.ident` for the records of *this* import, but it is looked up with `c.id`, the id the `similar` index returns for a candidate — and the index is `[*base, *mine]`, i.e. stored records and import records live in one id space. Whenever a stored record and an import record share the same ident (exactly the id situation this change is told to coordinate with `B-fix-import-hyphen-ids`, and the normal case if a re-imported file yields the same idents it did the first time), the lookup resolves a queue candidate to the in-import record, and the guard `if not is_summary(f) or is_summary(tgt): continue` fires on the query itself. Given the file `X` already imported as lesson `L3 = "Use pnpm"` in the store, re-importing `X` yields an in-plan `L3 = "Use pnpm"`; `similar` returns the candidate with id `L3` (the query's own entry, or the stored one — they are indistinguishable), `tgt = in_plan["L3"]` is that `L3`, `is_summary(f) == is_summary(tgt)`, so the match is `continue`d and the identical record is **not** dropped; "re-importing the same file adds nothing" then fails, and `plan.duplicates`/the note omit it. When the colliding `tgt` is a *different* in-plan record (two imported records whose idents normalize to the same key), the same conflation mislabels a stored duplicate as `where == "import"` and `_resolve_chains` can leave `d.of` pointing at an intermediate record that is itself removed, so the operator is told to compare against an id that is never written. The fix is to distinguish queue vs. import candidates by which list the candidate came from (or to compare the object identity of `c` with `f`) rather than by an id lookup in a shared namespace.

chunk_findings.detail:
The cycle-guard seed is the wrong identifier, so the single chain hop the function exists to perform can be silently skipped and the note then points at a record that was *not* imported.

Walk through the only chain shape this code can produce. `_dedupe_found` accepts an in-import target only when `f` is a summary and the target is not, and a non-summary record can only be dropped against the queue, so the transitive case is exactly: summary `S` → non-summary `N` (this import) → queue record `Q`. `_resolve_chains` should rewrite `S`'s `of`/`where` from `N` to `Q`. It only does so when `nxt.of in seen` is false; `seen` is seeded with `d.found.ident` (which is `S.ident`), so the hop is skipped whenever the queue record's id equals `S`'s ident. That equality is explicitly contemplated by the marker comment two functions up — "a bug or an item can carry the same word" — i.e. a record of this import can share an id with a stored one.

Concretely: import file yields summary lesson with `ident == "L7"`, and a non-summary lesson `N` (ident `"L9"`) that is a near-duplicate of the stored lesson `Q` whose id is also `"L7"`. `S` is identical to `N`, so `dS.duplicate` is created with `of="L9"`, `where="import"`, `identical=True`. In `_resolve_chains`, `nxt = dropped[id(N)]`, `nxt.of == "L7"`, and `"L7" in {"L7"}` → `break`, so `dS.of` stays `"L9"` and `dS.where` stays `"import"`. The operator-facing note then reads `L7 = L9 (in this import)`, naming a record that `plan.found` just had filtered out, instead of `L7 = L7` (the held record). The function's own contract ("point at the record that is actually held") is violated, and `d.identical`/`d.score` are also left un-ANDed/un-min'ed against `nxt`, so an identical-with-follow-up case can be reported in the "word for word" bucket when the actually-held target is only a near-duplicate. Seeding `seen` with `d.of` (the first target) instead of `d.found.ident` fixes both.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/importer.py:2834` (`_resolve_chains`, `seen = {d.found.ident}`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The stored bug's text is written as `"Never force a push to a shared branch\nForce pushing rewrites history other worktrees are built on; use a revert commit instead."`. In the source, `\n` is an escaped backslash followed by `n`, i.e. a literal two‑character `
`, not a line break. The lesson it is supposed to duplicate (`L2` in `LESSONS`) is authored as a heading line, a blank line, then the body, and the importer represents records as `Found(kind, ident, title, source, body=…)` with title/body split on the newline (that is exactly how `L1`/`L2` get their titles in tests 1–5). A bug whose `summary` contains no real newline therefore yields `title = "Never force a push to a shared branch
Force pushing … instead."` (the whole blob) and `body = ""`, so it no longer resembles `L2`'s `title="Never force a push to a shared branch"` / `body="Force pushing … instead."`; the near-dup score falls under the 0.55 threshold, `plan.duplicates` comes back empty, and `(dup,) = plan.duplicates` raises `ValueError` before the id-collision behaviour the test exists to check is ever exercised. Using `"
"` (single backslash) would make the summary split the same way `L2` does and restore the intended queue match `("L2", "L2", "queue")`.

chunk_findings.detail: The direction guard is applied unconditionally to every candidate that comes from this import, so *two records of the same import that are identical (or near-identical) to each other and are not tagged `summary` are both kept*. Given an onboarding file that lists the same lesson text twice (neither tagged `summary`), `mine` contains both; for the first record the candidate `rec(second)` is an import candidate, `is_summary(first)` is False, so the loop hits `continue`, skips it, finds no other qualifying candidate, and leaves the record in `plan.found`. The second record behaves symmetrically. The result is that both are imported (and neither is listed in `plan.duplicates`), which contradicts the stated intent "Import skips identical text" and the function's own promise that the outcome does not depend on how records were read. The same `continue` also silently swallows the near-duplicate sibling case, so a pair of near-identical non-summary records inside one file is neither dropped nor reported to the onboarding conversation. The guard's rationale ("a summary bullet repeats the corpus, never the reverse") justifies ordering summary-vs-corpus, but identical text has no direction, so it should still be collapsed to one record regardless of the `summary` tag.
